title: In vitro differentiation of human embryonic stem cells to hemogenic endothelium and blood progenitors via embryoid body formation
protocol: Thaw a Geltrex aliquot on ice for 10–12 hours in a fridge.
Prepare a 1:40 dilution of the thawed Geltrox with cold KO-DMEM, resulting in a total dilution factor from initial stock of 1:200.
Dispense 1 mL of diluted Geltrex per well of a 6-well plate.
Place the 6-well plate with Geltrox at 37°C for 15–20 minutes.
Check under the microscope that Geltrox pieces have attached, then aspirate any remaining Geltrox.
Wash gently each well with 1–2 mL of KO-DMEM.
Add 1 mL of TeSR-E8 basal medium per well.
Leave TeSR-E8 medium at 20°C for at least 30 minutes to warm up.
Place an aliquot of EDTA 0.5 mM solution in a 37°C water bath for at least 10 minutes prior to use.
Prepare the required volume of TeSR-E8 medium containing 10 μM ROCK inhibitor, calculating 1.5 mL per well.
Carefully remove the medium from hESC colonies.
Wash quickly and gently with 0.5 mL of EDTA 0.5 mM to remove any trace of medium and debris.
Add 1 mL of EDTA 0.5 mM and place cells in the incubator at 37°C for 2 minutes.
Check colonies under microscope; observe relaxed cell-cell interactions and more refringent cells within colonies.
Carefully remove EDTA solution without disturbing the cell layer.
Let cells dry by keeping plate lid off for 1 minute in tissue culture hood.
Pipette 500 μl of TeSR-E8 medium containing ROCK inhibitor directly over colonies to detach small clumps of 5–6 cells.
Repeat step until reaching desired volume of medium, calculating 500 μl per well for hESC split.
Dispense 500 μl of hESC clump suspension dropwise to each new well.
Gently move plate up and down, left and right to evenly distribute cell clumps within wells.
Transfer plate to an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2 in normoxia.
Replace medium without ROCK inhibitor after 24 hours.
Observe hESC colonies grown on Geltrex-coated dishes for morphology changes.
Make a stock of hESCs grown on Geltrex before beginning an experiment if needed.
Warm up an aliquot of EDTA solution in a water bath at 37°C for at least 10 minutes.
Determine the volume of freezing medium needed, calculating 1 mL per cryovial.
Use freezing medium instead of TeSR-E8 medium in step j of the EDTA passage protocol.
Transfer cell clumps into cryovials after treatment with freezing medium.
Place cryovials in a freezing container filled with isopropanol or similar to ensure gradual temperature decrease.
Store freezing container at -80°C.
Transfer cryovials to liquid nitrogen 24–48 hours later.
When hESCs reach 80% confluence, form embryoid bodies (EBs) for differentiation.
Culture small aggregates of hESCs in the presence of BMP4 for 24 hours to promote survival.
Add ROCK inhibitor and Geltrex at day 0 to enhance cell survival and aggregation.
At day 1, add FGF2 to the EB medium.
Change the medium on days 2 and 4.
Remove TeSR-E8 medium from hESC cultures.
Wash each well of a 6-well plate quickly with 1 mL of EDTA 0.5 mM.
Incubate at 37°C for 2 minutes or until colony edges appear refractive under the microscope.
Aspirate EDTA and replace with 2 mL of IMDM 20% FBS EB harvesting medium.
Cut hESC colonies into small clumps using a StemPro EZPassage tool, cutting up and down and rotating the plate to cut in a perpendicular orientation.
Grow hESC colonies on Geltrex-coated dishes.
Cut the colonies into small squares using a StemPro EZPassage tool for embryoid body seeding.
Collect the clumps in a screw-cap tube, avoiding single cell suspension by gentle pipetting.
Wash the plate thoroughly with extra medium to harvest all clumps.
Use a cell scraper to reach cells at the edges of the well.
Let the clumps settle by gravity for 20 min.
If clumps are small, centrifuge them for 5 min at 600 × g.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant.
Gently add 2 ml (per well of a 6-well plate) or 10 ml (per 10 cm dish) of Embryoid Body differentiation medium day 0.
Transfer clumps to Poly-HEMA coated plates.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% O₂, and 5% CO₂.
On day 1, add 0.5 ml per well or 2 ml per 10 cm dish of EB medium day 0 containing FGF2 for a final concentration of 5 ng/mL in the total volume.
On day 2, collect the EBs with a 10 ml serological pipette and let them settle by gravity for 15-20 min.
Gently wash the dish with 6 ml of IMDM basal medium to collect all EBs.
Resuspend the EBs in EB medium day 2.
Replate the EBs in new Poly-HEMA-coated dishes or plates.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% O₂, and 5% CO₂.
On day 4, collect the EBs and let them settle by gravity for 15–20 minutes.
Resuspend the settled EBs in EB medium day 4.
Replate the resuspended EBs into new Poly-HEMA-coated dishes or plates.
Incubate the re-plated EBs at 37°C with 5% O2 and 5% CO2 for two more days.
Once the EBs are pelleted, carefully remove the supernatant.
Add 5 mL of warm TrypLE per 50 mL tube.
Incubate for 3 min at 37°C in a water bath.
Vortex briefly after incubation.
Return to the water bath for 2 min if EB clumps remain.
Add 5 mL IMDM 10% FBS and pipette up and down to disaggregate EBs.
Pass supernatant through a pre-wet 50 μm Filcon filter into 5 mL snap cap tubes.
Add 2 mL IMDM 10% FBS to remaining EBs.
Use a 5 mL syringe with a 18G blunt needle to disaggregate remaining clumps.
Pass supernatant through a pre-wet Filcon filter into 5 mL snapcap tubes until all EBs are collected.
Count cells using a hematocytometer.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 3,000 × g.
Resuspend cells in IMDM 10% FBS at 5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Pass the cell solution through a pre-wet 50 μm Filcon filter to remove potential clumps.
Set aside 200 μL of cell suspension for flow cytometry unstained control and single stained controls.
Stain the cell solution with anti-CD43, anti-CD144, and anti-CD31 antibodies.
Add Hoechst 33258 as a live/death discriminator.
Stain between 20 × 10^6 and 50 × 10^6 cells.
Incubate for 1 hour at 4°C, mixing the cell solution after 30 minutes by vortexing gently.
Wash cells once with 5 mL of IMDM 10% FBS.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 3,000 × g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in IMDM 10% FBS at 5 × 10^6 cells/mL or less depending on the Flow Cytometer sorter used.
Perform compensation settings using BD CompBeads labeled with antibodies according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Decide gating strategy based on unstained and single stained cell samples.
Sort live cells positive for CD144 and CD31 expression and negative for CD43 expression.
Centrifuge sorted cells for 5 minutes at 3,000 × g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells at 1 × 10^6 cells/mL in hemogenic endothelium inducing medium.
Plate cells on gelatin-coated plates at 120,000 cells per well of a 6-well plate for analysis at day 4.
Plate cells on gelatin-coated plates at 80,000 cells for analysis at day 7.
Warm up TrypLE solution in a water bath at 37°C before starting.
Collect the supernatant of the culture into a 15 mL screw-cap tube.
Add 1 mL of warm TrypLE to the well.
Incubate for 3 min at 37°C in an incubator.
Gently detach and resuspend cells by pipetting up and down.
Transfer detached cells to the tube containing the supernatant.
Wash the well with 1 mL of IMDM 10% FBS.
Centrifuge the cell mixture for 3 min at 3,000 × g.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of FACS wash.
Stain cells for hematopoietic markers (CD43, CD235a).
Stain cells for endothelial markers (KDR, CD73).
Analyze a set of 1 × 10^5 to 5 × 10^5 stained cells.
Include unstained control in the analysis.
Perform compensation settings using BD CompBeads labeled with antibodies.
Run fluorescence minus one (FMO) controls for multicolor flow cytometry panels.
Warm an aliquot of methylcellulose (MEC) at 37°C for at least 20 min.
Prepare the required amount of semi-solid medium, adding the methylcellulose last using a 5 ml syringe with 18G blunt needle.
Dispense 3.5 ml of semi-solid medium per 15 ml snapcap tube using a 5 ml syringe with 18G blunt needle.

Add 3.5 × 10^3 to 10^5 cells of day 4 or day 7 hemogenic culture to each 15 ml snapcap tube containing 3.5 ml of semi-solid medium and vortex vigorously briefly to homogenously mix the cells within the methylcellulose medium.
Let the air bubbles settle.
Incubate for 5 min in a 37°C water bath to loosen up the methylcellulose and vortex vigorously to mix and allow the air bubbles to dissipate before dispensing.
Using a 1 ml syringe and 18G blunt needle, carefully distribute 1 ml of the solution per 35 mm sterile petri dish.
Place the dishes in a cell culture protective tray.
Add water to the tray to maintain appropriate humidity.
Put the tray with dishes into an incubator set at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 5% O2.
Maintain an appropriate level of water inside the tray for two weeks.
Count colonies after 14 days of culture.
Mitotically inactivate OP9 stromal cells expressing human DLL1 using Mitomycin C.

Plate a vial containing 10^6 mitotically inactivated OP9-hDLL1-GFP mouse stromal cells in a 12-well plate or a 6-well plate in OP9-DLL1 medium, depending on the number of cell populations to be tested.
Check that the OP9-hDLL1 cells are healthy and homogenously distributed one day after plating.
Warm up an aliquot of the OP9-DLL1 medium at 20°C.
Harvest cells after 4 days of hemogenic inducing culture if necessary.
Seed cells at minimum of 10^4 cells per cm² in T lymphoid generation medium containing cytokines.
Transfer cells to a fresh inactivated OP9-hDLL1 layer at day 10 and every 5 days thereafter.
Feed the cells with stroma medium containing cytokines from day 15 onward.
Collect supernatant into a tube before passage.
Add 1 ml of warm TrypLE to the well and incubate for 3 minutes at 37°C.
Gently detach and resuspend the cells by pipetting up and down.
Transfer detached cells to the tube containing the collected supernatant.
Wash the well with 1 ml of stroma medium.
Pass the mixture through a pre-wet 50 μm sterile Filcon.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 3,000 × g.
Add fresh OP9-DLL1 medium containing human cytokines according to the day of culture.
Transfer each well completely to another well to maintain the culture without diluting the cell density.
Dissociate the culture after 1 month in culture as described for passaging.
Analyze the cells by flow cytometry for the expression of human CD45, CD8, and CD4 markers.
Use Hoechst 33258 or any other suitable live dye for live/dead discrimination.
